comments.text: Read the request byte $142F. Its high bit initialises the SID and 81 bytes of voice state, then selects six split voice-sequence pointer bytes from one of seven starts and retains the low three voice-enable bits. Otherwise process each enabled voice.
Seven offsets, spaced by six bytes, into the tune-start table at $14A7.

Set volume/filter mode $1F. Fetch sequence and pattern bytes using per-voice indices. Sequence $FE restarts and $FF mutes envelopes then restarts; high-bit sequence bytes set transpose. Pattern low bits select note, instrument, duration and effect commands. Continue into envelope, waveform, pulse, pitch and filter updates.

End a note at its duration boundary, skip muted voices and clear envelopes for instrument zero. Otherwise select a ten-byte instrument record at $1530 plus ten times instrument-minus-one, write attack/decay and sustain/release, and choose the phase-dependent control value.
Initialise pulse modulation from instrument bytes six and seven, retain pulse limits and flags, then send the instrument's attack control value to the voice.
Update each voice's pulse-width accumulator, direction and step acceleration according to its instrument. Write the low pulse byte and continue to the high pulse byte and pitch processing.

Write the pulse high byte. An arpeggio instrument cycles offsets from byte eight; otherwise the first note tick uses note plus transpose. Read split frequency tables and write the voice frequency registers, then apply vibrato or slide.
Prefer the explicit pattern pitch effect when present. Otherwise decode instrument vibrato depth, delay and speed, update its direction flags, and select upward or downward frequency addition.
Add the voice's pitch step to its sixteen-bit frequency accumulator one more time than the loop index, emitting frequency writes on each iteration.
Subtract the voice's pitch step from its sixteen-bit frequency accumulator one more time than the loop index, emitting frequency writes on each iteration.

For qualifying instrument flags, run a sixteen-step waveform/frequency-high sequence. Update the voice's filter-routing bit and optionally step through the 48-byte cutoff table. Advance the note age and continue with the next enabled voice.
Low bytes of 96 chromatic note frequencies; paired with $136C.
High bytes of 96 chromatic note frequencies; paired with $130C.
SID register offsets zero, seven and fourteen for the three voices.
Per-voice filter-routing bits one, two and four.
Per-voice masks $FE, $FD and $FB remove one routing bit while preserving the other bits.
48 filter-cutoff-high values stepped by the music driver at $12FD.
Overlapping waveform and frequency-high effect tables, read at offsets $1461 and $1471 with phase plus zero or 32; 16 steps per mode.
Frequency-high adjustments paired with the waveform sequence; overlapping entries are selected by the same mode-dependent phase.
Three low bytes of the active voice-sequence pointers, copied from the selected start record by music initialisation.
Three high bytes of the active voice-sequence pointers, paired with $14A1.
Seven six-byte start records: three low voice pointers then three high voice pointers. Request $87 selects record zero and all voices.
32 low pattern pointer bytes, paired with high bytes at $14F1.
32 high pattern pointer bytes, paired with low bytes at $14D1.
Eleven ten-byte instrument records. Bytes 0-3 select gate timing and waveform controls, 4-5 the SID envelopes, 6-7 pulse behaviour, 8-9 pitch and filter behaviour; reader $0FB5.
First voice sequence: high-bit bytes set transposition, low bytes select patterns, $FE restarts the sequence. Selected by start record zero.
Second voice sequence, using repeated pattern nine and pattern eleven before the $FE loop marker.
Third voice sequence for the title start: pattern ids three to six and eleven, ending with $FE.
